newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition floods telcom law with amendments.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition floods telcom law with amendments.

text.p: Italian opposition parties on Tuesday filed more than 6,000 amendments to a government bill for the creation of an authority to regulate the telecoms sector.
The bill, which must be passed into law for the privatisation of telecoms holding Stet to go ahead, has first to be approved by the upper house (Senate) communications committee.
It then goes before a full session of the Senate before passing to the Chamber of Deputies for a final reading.
Far-right Alleanza Nazionale and Forza Italia presented most of the amendments. The hard-left Communist Refoundation put forward more than 50.

Undersecretary Michele Lauria said that a strong political consensus was needed to overcome the obstacles to the approval of the draft law. "Without a strong and wide political clarification I see numerous obstacles to the approval of the law," he said in a statement.
But he added the privatisation of Stet would go ahead as planned. The government planned the sell-off between February 1 and March 31, 1997.
The government has repeatedly said the bill should be approved by both houses of parliament by the end of the year in order for the sell-off to proceed. -- Rome newsroom 392-6782505
